questions.question_text: A water meter showed a reading of $1417\text{ kL}$ at the start of a billing cycle and $1482\text{ kL}$ at the end. How many kilolitres of water were consumed during the cycle?

options.why: Takes the final meter reading instead of calculating the difference between readings.
Makes an arithmetic subtraction error when calculating $1482 - 1417$.
Adds the two meter readings together instead of subtracting the previous reading.
Omits the $10\%$ GST calculation on the subtotal.
Adds \$10 instead of computing $10\%$ of \$390.00 as GST.
Applies GST only to the usage charge and neglects the supply charge entirely.

questions.question_text: A water account includes a water usage charge of $58\text{ kL}$ at \$2.30 per kL, a water service charge of \$42.50, and a sewerage service charge of \$148.00. Water and sewerage services are GST-free. What is the total charge for the water account?

options.why: Calculates the usage charge but omits the fixed service charges.
Incorrectly adds $10\%$ GST to GST-free residential water services.
Adds only the fixed service charges and omits the usage charge.

questions.question_text: A gas account shows $6500\text{ MJ}$ of consumption at $3.0\text{ cents per MJ}$ and a daily supply charge of \$0.80 per day for $60$ days (both excluding GST). What is the total amount payable including $10\%$ GST?

options.why: Omits the $10\%$ GST on the subtotal.
Includes GST on the usage charge but omits the daily supply charge.
Multiplies $6500 \times 0.30$ instead of $0.03$, misconverting cents to dollars.

questions.question_text: A monthly telecommunications bundle increased in price from \$75.00 to \$84.00. What is the percentage increase?

options.why: Confuses the dollar increase of \$9.00 with a percentage.
Divides the \$9 increase by the new amount \$84 instead of the original \$75.
Calculates the ratio of new to old bill without subtracting $100\%$.

questions.question_text: A quarterly electricity bill lists a total energy consumption of $1820\text{ kWh}$ across a $91$-day billing cycle. What was the average daily electricity consumption?

options.why: Divides by $100$ instead of the actual billing duration of $91$ days.
Divides by $11$ instead of $91$ days.
Divides by $30$ days assuming a standard month instead of $91$ days.

questions.question_text: An electricity account for a $90$-day period has a total amount due of \$350.90 including $10\%$ GST. The daily supply charge is \$0.90 per day (ex GST) and energy is billed at $28\text{ cents per kWh}$ (ex GST). How many kilowatt-hours ($\text{kWh}$) were consumed?

options.why: Calculates usage directly from the GST-inclusive total without dividing by $1.10$.
Forgets to subtract the supply charge from the pre-GST subtotal before dividing by the unit rate.
Divides the GST-inclusive total directly by the unit rate without removing GST or supply charge.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Pre-GST subtotal} = \dfrac{\$350.90}{1.10} = \$319.00$
$\text{Supply charge} = 90 \times \$0.90 = \$81.00$
$\text{Usage charge} = \$319.00 - \$81.00 = \$238.00$
$\text{Usage in kWh} = \dfrac{\$238.00}{\$0.28}$
$= 850\text{ kWh}$

questions.question_text: A $3$-person household used $54\text{ kL}$ of water over a $90$-day billing period. The water-efficiency benchmark for their property size is $180\text{ L per person per day}$. Which statement correctly describes their daily water consumption ($1\text{ kL} = 1000\text{ L}$)?

options.text: They used $200\text{ L per person per day}$, exceeding the target by $20\text{ L}$.
They used $600\text{ L per person per day}$, exceeding the target by $420\text{ L}$.
options.why: Calculates total household daily litres but fails to divide by the 3 occupants.

options.text: They used $0.2\text{ L per person per day}$, meeting the target by $179.8\text{ L}$.
options.why: Omits the conversion from kilolitres to litres, dividing $54\text{ kL}$ directly by $90$ days and $3$ occupants to get $0.2\text{ L per person per day}$.

options.text: They used $200\text{ L per person per day}$, which meets the target.
options.why: Identifies the correct usage rate of 200 L/person/day but misinterprets it as being below the 180 L target.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total litres} = 54 \times 1000 = 54\,000\text{ L}$
$\text{Household daily usage} = \dfrac{54\,000}{90} = 600\text{ L/day}$
$\text{Usage per person} = \dfrac{600}{3} = 200\text{ L/person/day}$
$\text{Difference from benchmark} = 200 - 180$
$= 20\text{ L (exceeds target)}$
